objective: Make account deactivation and permanent deletion durable, prevent deleted-subject resurrection, and automatically reconcile accepted deletion work without depending on a browser or password-reset changes.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: the Director specification/scope PR defining USERS-009 and merged ADR 0009 are ancestors of fresh origin/main before authoring unit tests. AUTH-001 and its parked experiment remain stopped and untouched. No task-state changes belong in the Director prerequisite. Test-first: commit failing tests alone, implementation separately; no dependency additions or policy expansion.

Add durable account authority keyed uniquely by configured trusted issuer/pool plus immutable Cognito sub, never email, alias or profile id. Every new table has a bigint identity primary key. Authority holds active/inactive/deleting/deleted state, monotonic generation, original inactive timestamp and minimal retained deletion identity. Its lifetime is independent of User; deleting/deleted cannot transition back to active/inactive or be removed with profile cleanup. Validate namespace consistently across API, consumers, reconciler and perf-only verifier configuration.

Add durable lifecycle operation and exact-owned-object manifest records. An accepted deletion has exactly one immutable server operation identity per subject for its deletion lifetime; duplicate DELETE calls resume/report it without creating a new intent or resetting completed stages. Deactivation/recovery record their state transition atomically with a minimal operation result. No request payload may choose the acting subject. Store no passwords/codes/tokens/email or provider exception bodies; opaque external operation handles must not expose bigint keys.

Before any destructive external call, atomically commit deleting authority, operation, generation and cleanup manifest/work record. Snapshot owned post/media identifiers and every exact stored or deterministic possible quarantine/public output key through module interfaces under consistent locking. Manifest ownership and configured bucket identity are immutable after acceptance; do not accept arbitrary bucket/key input or broad-prefix deletion. Local DB work record is the durable outbox: no queue or notification delivery is required for recovery.

Enforce authority on authenticated dependencies, profile creation and all mutation commit boundaries, including no-profile paths and optional identity reads. Deleting/deleted callers cannot recreate a profile, recover, upload, publish, follow, like, report or change preferences. Inactive own-account recovery/deactivation and guest-read semantics stay compatible. Failure to read authority fails closed for authenticated use; anonymous guest reads and /health remain available. Narrow same-sub status/permanent-deletion retry paths alone may authenticate an otherwise valid old ID token for a tombstoned subject; they grant no general mutation authority.

Serialize lifecycle acceptance and concurrent actor mutations through the stable authority record, including when User no longer exists. Recheck/fence generation at commit, not only dependency entry. Define one lock order covering authority, user, post and media rows; test competing acceptance, profile creation, recover/delete and mutation commits in real PostgreSQL without sleeps. A mutation that wins before acceptance is included in the snapshot; one that loses cannot commit afterward. Existing module boundaries are preserved.

Background media publication and notification writes consult users public lifecycle interfaces, use the same fencing/lock order, and cannot recreate local personal rows or publish active content after deleting. Fence affected recipient/actor/owner identities deterministically; preserve unrelated authors replies/reposts and existing anonymous post tombstones. Late media external writes receive compensation and remain covered by the retained manifest. An expired lease or Lambda/client timeout is not proof an old external request ended.

Use one shared stage-specific deletion runner for the HTTP attempt and a scheduled reconciler: exact-key S3 cleanup with per-key error checks, local personal-data removal in one module-owned transaction, exact-sub Cognito AdminDeleteUser last. Persist stage/evidence before advancing; crash or ambiguous outcome keeps unfinished work. Retry S3 deletion and exact-sub identity removal safely; UserNotFound is completion evidence only for that identity stage, never for unfinished S3/DB work. No global sign-out/reset orchestration is introduced. A stale worker cannot regress state or clear a newer generation.

Keep DELETE /users/me/data compatible: recent auth_time within five minutes is required at intent acceptance/retry, caller-only identity path, and 204 only after S3 current cleanup, local removal and provider deletion stages are durably complete. Never return 202/other success while unfinished because current frontend treats any success as deletion complete. An accepted-but-pending/failed attempt returns generic 503 retryable status with Retry-After and the same opaque operation handle/Location; no sensitive stage diagnostics. Preserve repeated completion and provider-absent idempotency. No frontend session clearing or deletion-success announcement occurs on a pending/error response.

Add GET /users/me/data-operation, before the dynamic /users/{user_id} route, authenticated by a cryptographically valid matching issuer/sub token without requiring a profile. Return only the owners opaque operation_id and generic in_progress/retrying/completed status; 404 when that owner has no operation. Do not accept user ids/subjects or expose object keys, provider diagnostics or another owners status; unauthenticated/expired tokens remain 401. This is an additive API, not a new frontend polling experience or an unauthenticated capability endpoint. Regenerate OpenAPI and TypeScript schema.

Automatic reconciliation must progress all known accepted work after browser loss, response loss, worker crash, missing wakeups or lease expiry. A bounded, paginated DB scan claims due work using safe fencing, bounded retries/backoff/jitter, fair ordering and bounded external-call work per invocation; poison work does not starve other subjects. Lease age only permits inspection/retry, never unlocks an account or proves completion. Retain terminal tombstone manifests and schedule periodic exact-key cleanup of late presigned uploads/late provider writes; do not discard this obligation at a timer threshold.

Create a dedicated VPC-backed image Lambda handler app.account_deletion_handler.handler with an EventBridge scheduled Rule every five minutes, least-privilege invocation permission, bounded timeout, DB-claimed-work concurrency control and existing alarm-topic integration. Preserve the pinned no-reserved-concurrency invariant: correctness lives in PostgreSQL locks/fencing, not an account-level Lambda quota. Add the reconciler Errors and Throttles alarms and deliberately update infra/test/alarms.test.ts pinned function/alarm count and rationale without weakening coverage. Handler opens/closes its own session and invokes the same runner/scan without impersonating a user. Restrict its role to existing DB/network/KMS/log requirements, exact configured media object resources and exact Cognito pool AdminDeleteUser; no user listing, password APIs, SES, broad invoke or queue. Use existing IAM boundary/execution-policy ceilings only if synthesized tests prove coverage; any missing ceiling requires a separate human-reviewed Director prerequisite before the unit proceeds.

Wire explicit schema-ready activation and trusted issuer/pool settings consistently for API, media, notifications and reconciler. Add an additive single-head migration and evidence-based backfill for extant profiles preserving inactive timestamps. Do not reconstruct historical deleted subjects from absent rows or silently enroll a pre-cutover no-profile identity. The concrete legacy inventory/adoption and cutover/drain plan requires separate human review before activation; unresolved legacy ambiguity is a release blocker, not permission to lock legitimate incomplete-signup accounts. Dormant schema/code deployment is not a completed security rollout, and activation cannot fall back to legacy deletion or raw-JWT acceptance when schema/provider/adoption evidence is unavailable.

Tests cover every stage crash/rollback and automatic retry, stale-worker/duplicate/concurrent delivery, deleted-sub profile recreation, same email/new sub isolation, no-profile retry, cross-owner status, unauthenticated/expired status, recent-auth boundaries, inactivity recovery, transaction-level mutations/consumer races, current S3 partial errors, late known-key writes and non-versioned storage assumptions. No finite timing experiment establishes external completion. The deployment gate separately verifies live quarantine/public buckets remain unversioned; unexpected versioning blocks activation pending a reviewed version-cleanup/IAM plan. No DeleteObjectVersion permission is added speculatively.

Keep current erasure scope honest: 204 establishes logical app/identity deletion and successful current exact-object cleanup, not instantaneous removal from CDN/backups or a bound on in-flight remote writes. Retained manifests automatically remove later known-key arrivals; current one-day quarantine lifecycle and seven-day DB backup retention remain separate obligations, and CDN cache retention must be evidenced. Inventory and exact warning/copy changes, if necessary, require a separately scoped frontend/Director follow-up before activation; do not silently strengthen the existing all-data-deleted promise.

Director independently runs applicable full backend/frontend container suites, infra build/lint/test/synth and security review before the PR is ready; verify generated API compatibility and meaningful fault/race mutations. No AWS writes, production/user-data operation, deployment or migration invocation is authorized by this task spec. Future dev-provider/browser proof needs exact in-session approval and is evidence or NOT DONE. Record schedule cost, alarms and deployment gates in the PR; update Users/Posts/Media/Notifications module references, with Standards/FrontendUI changes on Director branches.
